newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates dip below double digits at close.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates dip below double digits at close.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates finished sharply lower on Wednesday as the market's recently tight liquidity began to show signs of easing after the central bank's fund injections, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate closed at 9.813 percent -- still far outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone but out of double digits for the first time since June 26 -- compared to Monday's 10.609 close.
The 30-day commercial paper had eased by the close to 7.50-8.00 percent from 9.25-9.75.
The market was closed on Tuesday on for banks' semiannual account settlement.
Taiwan's interbank rate had hovered above double digits in recent days, with funds cascading out of banks into the red-hot stock market.
The central bank, following three major liquidity injections last week, injected T$8.59 billion worth of funds into the banking system on Monday through open-market operations.
Dealers predicted more declines on Thursday.
The govenrment bond yields also went down on Wednesday.
The benchmark 86/4 bond yield was traded at a 5.8660-8730 percent range throughout the session against Monday's 5.8775-8780 close.
